text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- France and Germany do not intend to undertake any initiative on the Cyprus problem.
- Democratic Party (Diko) leader Spyros Kyprianou: our cooperation in the government is unshakeable.
- Talks between teachers and the education ministry on the status of private lessons reach a deadlock.
- The Democratic Party plans to stay in the coalition... for now.
- UN Secretary general calls for urgent efforts to halt 'worst violence since 1974'.
- Spyros Kyprianou leaves open the possibility of a 'divorce' with the government.
- Grey Wolves involvement in the killing of a Turkish Cypriot journalist is under investigation.
- The US is expected to come back with more insistence that its proposal for a ban on military flights be taken up.
- Nurses demands for better staffing levels in state-run hospitals are met.
- Turkish troops are on patrol a very short distance away from the national guard in Ayios Dhometios.
- Unrest is threatened in schools after a deadlock in negotiations between teachers and the education ministry.
- Diko and Edek parties will boycott events Malcolm Rifkind will attend during his visit on Monday.
